text: REST APIs allow different software systems to communicate over the internet. When designing one, you should follow some best practices. First, use clear and consistent endpoints, such as /users or /orders, so developers can easily understand them. Second, always return the correct status codes: for example, 200 for success, 404 when something is not found, and 500 for server errors. Third, provide good documentation that explains how each endpoint works, including request and response examples. Finally, use versioning, like /api/v1/, so you can update your API without breaking existing applications.
